newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips, bonds, dollar fall on strong data.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips, bonds, dollar fall on strong data.

text.p: Blue-ship stocks fell sharply Thursday as long-term bond interest rates shot up after a series of surprisingly strong economic reports, and the dollar weakened amid verbal attacks by German central bank officials.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 92.75 points, or 1.32 percent, at 6,927.38, one day after losing more than 47 points.
On Tuesday, it set a record high of 7,067.46 after closing for the first time above the 7,000 level last Thursday.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 1,679 to 840 on active volume of 490 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We've had day after day of stocks going up," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Now it appears some money managers are taking some chips off the table in the best-performing groups," he said.
Technology and financial stocks met with some of the stiffest selling, with the latter under extra pressure from a bond market decline.
Technology stocks turned in a particularly choppy performance, even when compared with an overall market that displays ever-increasing volatility by the day.

"We're in a stage of the market where volatility is going to remain quite high," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell. "There is a broad variety of opinions being expressed by market observers and at any given moment one camp will gain an upper hand.
"In technology, there may be the greatest degree of controversy about the profit outlook," he said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond fell nearly a full point, raising its yield to 6.65 percent from 6.58 percent Wednesday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The dollar, which has been flying higher for the past year, fell on signs of economic strength in Europe and more verbal attempts by German central bank officials to tame its recent strength.
Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer repeated his call for an end to its rise against the German mark.

The dollar fell to its lowest level since Feb. 10 against the Japanese yen, closing at 122.45 yen, more than two yen below 124.55 late Wednesday. Against the mark, the dollar fell to 1.6835 from 1.6980.
On New York's Commodity Exchange, the pace-setting April gold contract closed up $5 at $352.60 per ounce.

Crude oil prices fell as a weekly report showed ample domestic supplies and amid concerns that Iraq would increase sales. Crude oil for delivery in March closed 81 cents lower at $21.98 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange.

Overseas, London's FTSE finished down 1.3 points at 4,356.1 after having clambered to an all-time high of 4,362.4 in morning trade. In Tokyo, the Nikkei average of 225 leading issues rose 452.59 points or 2.43 percent to close at 19,051.71.
